svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.24.2.4 Openings in Fire Separations
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.24 SHEET STEEL STUD WALL FRAMING
Openings in Fire Separations

g.text: Door opening in a non-loadbearing fire separation
Door opening 1 200 mm wide or less
Door opening in a non-loadbearing fire separation
First stud 400 mm or less beyond the jamb, (3).
Supports 400 mm or less apart above the
opening when the space above is over 400 mm, (4)
Framing beside and over the door

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Where openings for doors in non-loadbearing
fire separations required to have a
fire-resistance rating do not exceed 1 200 mm
(3′-11¼″) in width,
(a) the width of steel studs is not less than 63
mm (2½″), and (b) the metal thickness is not less
Where openings described in Sentence (1)
exceed 1 200 mm in width,
(a) the width of steel studs is not less than 91
mm (3 9/16″), and (b) the metal thickness is not
less than 0.85 mm (0.033″).
The distance to the first stud beyond the jamb
of any door opening in a fire separation
required to have a fire-resistance rating does
not exceed 400 mm (15¾″).
Where the distance between the framing over
the opening referred to in Sentence (3) and
the top runner exceeds 400 mm in such walls,
intermediate support is installed at intervals
of not more than 400 mm above the opening.
Drawn: intermediate support shown as short studs on a runner over the opening. Sizes are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.24.2.4. (page 9-230)
